summary: Duplicate claims when a broker sends the same loss twice
description:
The claims centre found 23 pairs of identical claims last month. In each pair, both claims come from the same broker, for the same policy and the same loss date, a few seconds apart.

- The broker's system sends the claim, gets no answer within 10 seconds, and sends it again
- Intake creates two claim files
- An adjuster has to merge them by hand

Please fix before the hail season.

comments.author: p009
comments.text: intake has no idea it already saw the message. adding a check on broker id + policy + loss date + loss type, 24h window. the second one gets the first one's claim number back.

comments.author: p009
comments.text: in prod since this morning. 0 duplicates in a staging replay of may. closing.

summary: Access request: Pricing Engine needs read access to the Claims API
description:
System: Pricing Engine
Environment: production
Scope requested: claims.read

Why: since rating tables 2026.1, the number of claims in the last 5 years is a rating factor. Today we take that number from a monthly file out of the Data Warehouse, so a claim opened this week is not counted until next month. We want to call GET /claims?policy_id=... at quote time instead.

Volume: about 9,000 calls a day, with a peak of 40 a minute during broker hours.
Fields needed: claim id, loss date, loss type, status. No notes, no payment details.

I followed the steps in "Claims API: Access Guide".

comments.author: p006
comments.text: Approved. Read scope only, production. The credentials expire after 12 months, like for every client.

comments.author: p012
comments.text: Done. The client id is pricing-engine-prod, and the secret is in the vault under your team's path. The rate limit is 60 calls a minute. Please test in staging first: the v2 response has a few more fields than v1.

comments.author: p010
comments.text: Works in staging and in production. Thanks Sophie.

summary: Demande d'accès : le portail client doit lire et créer des réclamations (API Claims)
description:
Salut l'équipe Claims,

Pour Portail 2026, le client pourra déclarer une réclamation directement dans le portail et suivre son dossier. On a donc besoin d'un accès à l'API Claims v2 en production.

Système : Portail client
Scopes demandés : claims.read et claims.create
Volume : environ 300 créations et 5 000 lectures par jour

On est déjà branchés en staging depuis janvier et tout fonctionne. Le lancement est prévu le 15 juin, mais on aimerait tester en production bien avant.

Merci !

comments.author: p006
comments.text: Approved for claims.read and claims.create. Note for the Claims team: with the create scope, the portal must take the customer id from the session, never from the form.

comments.author: p018
comments.text: C'est fait. Client id : customer-portal-prod. J'ai limité claims.create aux réclamations du client connecté, comme demandé par David. Le secret est dans le coffre de votre équipe.

summary: Version 2 returns an error 500 for claims closed more than 7 years ago
description:
While testing in staging whether the Data Warehouse could load its claims from the Claims API instead of the nightly file, I get an error 500 from GET /v2/claims/{id} for some old claims.

- All of them were closed before April 2019
- The same ids worked with version 1
- Example: claim 2018-QC-0045512

It is not blocking, because I can skip them. But the answer should be a clear message, not a 500.

comments.author: p024
comments.text: What I checked so far: the claim exists in the database, and the Workbench opens it without a problem. The error comes from the API only. Claims closed for more than 7 years are moved to the archive tables, and version 2 never reads the archive.

comments.author: p024
comments.text: Fixed. Version 2 now reads the archive too, and marks those claims with archived: true. I also added a test with a 2018 claim, so that it cannot come back. Sophie reviewed the change.

summary: Access request: service account for the Broker Portal on the Claims API
description:
Brokers keep calling the claims centre to ask where their client's claim is. We want to show the claim status in the Broker Portal.

System: Broker Portal
Environment: production
Scope: claims.read, limited to the claims of the broker's own clients

This is a service account, not a person: the portal calls the API for the broker who is logged in.

Target: live before the end of May.

comments.author: p006
comments.text: Approved, with one condition: the filter on the broker's own clients must be enforced by the API, not only by the portal.

comments.author: p018
comments.text: Done. Client id broker-portal-prod, scope claims.read, with the broker filter enforced by the API. The scope set is saved as "broker-read" so we can reuse it.

summary: Access request: fraud model batch job needs read access to claims
description:
System: Fraud Scoring Model (nightly scoring job)
Environment: production
Scope requested: claims.read

What we need
- The new claims of the day, once a night at 01:30, to score them.
- Fields: claim id, policy id, loss date, loss type, amount claimed, postal code of the loss.

What we don't need
- Adjuster notes, documents, payment details.

Today the job reads a file export that is often late (see DAT-70). Reading the API directly would remove that problem.

Volume: one batch a night, about 850 claims.

comments.author: p006
comments.text: Approved. Read only. Please keep the postal code out of any log file.

comments.author: p012
comments.text: Created fraud-model-prod. I reused the scope set Nadia defined for the Broker Portal in CLM-239 and removed the broker filter, so you get only the six fields you listed. The secret is in your team's vault path.

comments.author: p023
comments.text: Confirmed: the job ran against the API last night. Thank you.

summary: Show the fraud score on the claim summary screen
description:
Version 3 of the fraud scoring model writes a score for every new claim, but adjusters cannot see it. They only see a "flagged" label, with no reason.

Please show on the claim summary screen:
- the score, as a number between 0 and 1
- the three main reasons the model gives (for example "reported 40 days after the loss")
- a link to the page that explains how to read the score

Important: the screen must say that the score is a hint, not a decision.

comments.author: p024
comments.text: First version in staging. I tried three layouts with two adjusters. They preferred the reasons in plain words, without the number in big. So the number is small, and the reasons come first.

comments.author: p024
comments.text: Released with the checklist on 23 June. The text "This score is a hint. You decide." is under the score, in French and in English.

summary: The Workbench freezes when a claim has more than 200 documents
description:
Adjusters report that the Workbench freezes for one to two minutes when they open some claims.

- Only claims with many documents: photos, invoices, expert reports
- Worst case so far: a fire claim with 380 documents
- It started after the release of 9 June

Three adjusters lost notes they were typing. Priority high.

comments.author: p024
comments.text: Reproduced with a test claim of 250 documents. The summary screen loads a preview of every document before it shows anything. I am changing it to load the first 20, then the rest when the adjuster scrolls.

comments.author: p024
comments.text: Released on 23 June. A claim with 380 documents now opens in 2 seconds. Closing.

comments.author: p007
comments.text: Reopening. Same freeze again, on storm claims with more than 400 documents. The claims centre says it is not the summary screen this time, but the Documents tab.

comments.author: p024
comments.text: Hélène is right: I fixed the summary screen and not the Documents tab, which had the same problem. I should have checked both, sorry. The fix is ready and tested with 450 documents. It goes out with the release of 15 September.

comments.author: p024
comments.text: Released this morning. Both screens now load documents 20 at a time. Closing again.

summary: Access request: Data Warehouse nightly load from the Claims API
description:
System: Data Warehouse (nightly load)
Environment: production
Scope requested: claims.read

We load the claims every night from a file that Claims Platform exports at 23:00. We would like to read the Claims API instead, for two reasons:
1. The file has no closed-date field, so the reports on closed claims are wrong.
2. When the export is late, the whole load is late.

Volume: one run a night, about 6,000 changed claims a day.
Window: 00:15 to 01:15, before the fraud job at 01:30.

comments.author: p006

comments.author: p024

Claims operations sent the new limits on 24 July. They must be live in the Workbench before 1 September.

comments.author: p007

summary: Claims from the phone line arrive without a policy number
description:
Since the phone system update of 24 August, about one claim in three taken by phone arrives in Claims Intake with an empty policy number.

- The agent types the policy number during the call, and it shows on their screen

comments.text:
Found it. Calls taken on the new agent screen (about a third of them so far) send the policy number as policyNo, and intake still reads policy_number. Calls on the old screen, and portal and broker messages, are not affected.

The claims centre has matched most of them to a policy by hand, but nobody can change that field in the Workbench once the file exists. I am writing a script to fill it in from the call records.

description:
The nightly export from the Legacy Policy System to the Policy Database has failed 3 nights in a row (4, 5, and 6 April).

Vous avez vu juste : le traitement de nuit du système patrimonial conserve sa propre liste de certificats, laquelle n'est pas mise à jour par l'équipe d'infrastructure, puisqu'elle ne se trouve pas sur ses serveurs. summary: Add endorsements to the policy details response
description:
GET /policies/{id} returns the policy as it was issued. The changes made during the term (endorsements) are missing, so clients such as the Customer Portal show the wrong coverage after a change.

Add an endorsements array to the response:

    "endorsements": [
      {"number": 2, "effective_date": "2025-03-01", "type": "vehicle_change", "premium_change": 41.50}
    ]

Rules
- Ordered by effective date
- Cancelled endorsements are not returned
- Nothing changes for clients that ignore the new field

comments.author: p020
comments.text: Released in Policy API 3.4. Response time for a policy with 20 endorsements: 38 ms before, 44 ms after. The contract tests are updated.

summary: Update the flood-zone decline rule after the spring floods
description:
The floods of April showed that our flood map is out of date. We insured 140 homes last year in streets that were under water this spring.

Samuel, please update the rule that declines new home policies in flood zones:
- use the province's 2026 flood map
- the rule works by postal code today. Check whether that is still precise enough
- existing customers are not affected: the rule is for new policies only

I approve the change before it goes live.

comments.author: p021
comments.text: The 2026 map adds 212 postal codes to the high-risk list and removes 31. A full postal code is precise enough in towns. In the country it is not: one rural postal code can cover both a riverbank and a hill. For 18 rural codes, I suggest "send to an underwriter" instead of "decline".

comments.author: p005
comments.text: Approved, including the 18 rural codes sent to an underwriter.

comments.author: p021
comments.text: Live since this morning. Tested on last year's 140 flooded homes: 131 would now be declined or sent to an underwriter.

summary: Quotes fail with "territory not found" for new Quebec postal codes
description:
Three brokers called this morning. They can't get a car or home quote for clients in some new housing developments north of Montreal. The Broker Portal shows "We could not price this risk".

In our logs the Pricing Engine answers:

    422 TERRITORY_NOT_FOUND postal_code=J7S 0B4

It seems to happen only with postal codes that start with J7S or J5P. Other J7 and J5 codes work.

Brokers are sending these clients to competitors. Please treat as urgent.

comments.author: p010
comments.text: Confirmed. J7S and J5P are new forward sortation areas (the first three characters of a postal code). The postal service added them in its August update. Our territory table only knows the areas that existed when rating tables 2026.2 were built, so the lookup finds nothing and the engine rejects the quote. The fix is in PRC-91.

comments.author: p010
comments.text: Fixed with rating tables 2026.3: both areas are mapped to territory QC-14. Quotes for J7S 0B4 and J5P 1A2 work in production. Resolving.

comments.author: p008
comments.text: Reopening. Same error again today, this time for G3P and J6G codes. Two brokers so far.

comments.author: p010
comments.text: Two more new areas, from the October postal update. I will add them today as an emergency table change, but we cannot keep doing this by hand every month. PRC-95 changes the engine so that an unknown area gets a fallback territory instead of an error.

comments.author: p005
comments.text: Approuvé pour les deux nouveaux secteurs, avec la même logique que dans PRC-91. Karim, même chose pour le journal des tables.

comments.author: p010
comments.text: G3P and J6G have been mapped since 21 October (tables 2026.3.1). I am keeping this open until PRC-95 is released, so that nobody thinks the problem is gone.

summary: Add the new Quebec postal code areas to the territory table (rating tables 2026.3)
description:
Follows PRC-88.

Change to the territory table:

    area  province  territory  note
    J7S   QC        QC-14      new, same territory as J7J and J7N around it
    J5P   QC        QC-14      new, same territory as J5L next to it

Why QC-14: both areas are new streets inside neighbourhoods that are already in QC-14. There is no claims history for them yet, so we use the territory around them. To review when we have 12 months of data.

Checklist from the mapping page:
- [x] rows added in staging
- [x] 20 test quotes per area, compared by hand
- [x] approval of the team lead
- [x] release as tables 2026.3

comments.author: p005
comments.text: Approuvé. D'accord pour QC-14 en attendant les données. Karim, ajoute une ligne dans le journal des tables pour l'audit, s'il te plaît.

comments.author: p010
comments.text: Released as 2026.3 at 07:40. Audit log line added.

summary: Use a fallback territory when a postal code area is unknown, instead of rejecting the quote
description:
Problem: every time the postal service adds an area, the engine rejects quotes until someone adds a row by hand (PRC-88, twice in six weeks).

Proposal
1. If the area (the first three characters) is unknown, use the territory of the nearest known area with the same first two characters.
2. Mark the quote with territory_source = "fallback", so that underwriting can see it.
3. Send one alert a day with the unknown areas, so that we still add them properly.

Not in scope: postal codes that do not exist at all. Those must still be rejected, with a clear message ("unknown postal code") instead of TERRITORY_NOT_FOUND.

Open question for Nathalie: is a fallback price acceptable to the actuaries, or do we need a loading on top?

comments.author: p005
comments.text: Les actuaires acceptent le repli sans majoration pendant 60 jours au maximum par secteur. Après, il faut une vraie ligne dans la table.

comments.author: p010
comments.text: Rules 1 and 2 are coded and in staging. The daily alert is next.

summary: Recalibrate the v2 score threshold after the false-positive spike
description:
The claims centre is complaining. In August, 11% of new claims were flagged for a fraud review, against 4% normally. Most of the flagged claims are hail damage from the storm of 14 August, and they are fine.

Tom, can you look at the threshold before the investigators drown?

comments.author: p011
comments.text: it's not the threshold per se. feature claim_cluster_7d fires on any geo cluster, storm or not. with a cat event you get hundreds of legit claims in the same area in 48h. precision at the 0.62 cutoff drops from 0.41 to 0.09 on august data.

comments.author: p011
comments.text: shipped: (1) cutoff 0.62 -> 0.64, (2) claim_cluster_7d is zeroed when the claim has a cat event code. flag rate back to 4.3% on september. recall on confirmed fraud basically flat (0.71 vs 0.72). the proper fix is retraining with event features, that's for v3.

summary: Hand over the fraud scoring model to Priya
description:
Tom is leaving us at the end of March. Priya takes over the fraud scoring model.

Before he goes:
- walk Priya through the training code and the nightly scoring job
- list everything that only Tom knows (there is a lot)

summary: Retrain the fraud scoring model with the claims up to 2025 (version 3)
description:
Goal: a version 3 of the fraud scoring model that handles weather events, so that a storm no longer floods the investigators (see DAT-52).

Scope
- Training data: claims opened from 2022 to 2025, with the result of the investigation
- New features: the event code, and the number of claims in the same area during the event
- Removed: claim_cluster_7d, which caused the false alerts

Done when
- The flag rate stays between 3% and 5% on the data of the August 2025 storm
- Recall on confirmed fraud is not lower than version 2 (0.71)
- The model overview and the runbook are written

comments.author: p023
comments.text: The first full retraining is finished, with Tom watching but not helping. Results on the 2025 hold-out data: flag rate 4.1%, recall 0.74, precision 0.44.

comments.author: p023
comments.text: Version 3 has been live since this morning. Version 2 keeps running in shadow mode for 30 days. The overview and runbook page is published.

summary: Nightly fraud feature job fails when the claims export is late
description:
The nightly scoring job starts at 01:30. It expects the claims export file from Claims Platform, which should arrive at 23:00.

Four times in April, the file arrived after 01:30. The job then fails without an alert, and the claims of that day get no fraud score until someone notices.

Expected: the job waits for the file, or it alerts us.

comments.author: p020
comments.text:
Two changes in the feature pipeline:
1. The job now waits up to 3 hours for the file, and alerts the data team channel after 30 minutes.
2. Claims without a score are picked up by the next run.
In production since last night.

comments.author: p020
comments.text: The fraud job now reads the Claims API directly (CLM-245), so the export file is no longer needed for scoring. Three weeks without a missed night. Closing.

summary: Weekly drift report for the fraud score
description:
Version 3 was trained on claims up to 2025. If the claims change (new kinds of fraud, a new product, a storm), the scores slowly become wrong and nobody sees it.

A weekly report, every Monday:
- the flag rate of the week, against the 3% to 5% band
- the distribution of the scores, against the training data
- the share of flagged claims that the investigators confirmed

An alert when the flag rate leaves the band two weeks in a row.

comments.author: p023
comments.text: The report has run for three Mondays. It is linked from the runbook. No alert so far.

summary: The warehouse has had no policy endorsements since June
description:
To prepare the quarterly pricing review, I compare the premium of each policy at the start of the quarter and today. For the third quarter so far (1 July to 21 August), the difference is zero for every policy, which cannot be right.

The table policy_endorsement has no rows after 14 June 2026. Before that date, there are about 900 a day.

comments.author: p020
comments.text: Confirmed. On 15 June the nightly load was moved to the new scheduler, and the endorsement step was left out of the new job definition. The job still ends in green, so nobody was alerted.

comments.author: p020
comments.text: The step has been back in the job since 27 August. I am reloading the missing endorsements month by month: June and July are done, and August is running. I am leaving this open until August is loaded and Samuel has checked his numbers.

summary: The build agents run out of disk space every Monday
description:
For the third Monday in a row, the first builds of the week fail with "No space left on device" on build agents 2 and 4.

- It fixes itself when someone cleans the agents by hand
- Our release of the Policy API was delayed by half a day today

Can the cleanup be automatic?

comments.author: p019
comments.text: tl;dr: the weekend security scan pulls every container image we own and never cleans up. Monday morning = full disks. I'm adding a cleanup at the end of the scan.

comments.author: p019
comments.text: Monday the 19th was clean. I also doubled the disks on agents 2 and 4, because why not. Closing.

summary: Private network link between the data centre and the cloud for the Policy Database migration
description:
For the migration we need to copy about 1.4 TB from the data centre to the cloud, then keep both sides in sync until the cutover.

Needs
- A private link, not the public internet
- At least 1 Gbps
- Only the two database servers on our side may use it

The plan is a first dry run in June.

comments.author: p022
comments.text: Circuit ordered from the carrier. Delivery date they gave: 2 March.

comments.author: p022
comments.text: Link is up. 1 Gbps, encrypted, two routes. The firewall rule allows only poldb-01 and poldb-02 to reach the cloud subnet. Measured 870 Mbps on a 50 GB test copy.

summary: Dry run 1 of the Policy Database cutover
description:
Action item from the steering committee of 18 March 2026.

Objective: rehearse the full cutover on a copy of production, and measure how long each step takes.

Owner: Wei Zhang
Support: Fatima Rahimi (network), Amira Khalil (Policy API checks)
Target date: week of 15 June 2026

Please attach the timings to this ticket for the next steering committee.

comments.author: p013
comments.text:
Dry run done on 17 June.

    step                   planned  actual
    stop writes            0:10     0:08
    final sync             0:45     1:32
    switch connections     0:20     0:25
    checks (Policy API)    0:30     0:41
    total                  1:45     2:46

It works, but the final sync takes twice the plan. One hour over is too much for a Saturday night window. The details are in the runbook.

comments.author: p017
comments.text: Thank you Wei. Added to the agenda of the next steering committee.

summary: Sign-in loops on the shared workstations of the claims centre
description:
Since Friday, adjusters on the shared workstations in Laval cannot sign in to the Workbench.

- They enter their password and the code from their phone
- The page comes back to the sign-in screen, again and again
- Their own laptops work
- 14 shared workstations, used by the evening shift

The evening shift is working on paper.

comments.author: p019
comments.text: tl;dr: clocks. The shared workstations are 7 minutes late, and since last week's update Single Sign-On refuses a sign-in when the clock is off by more than 5. Time sync was disabled on that workstation image, nobody knows why. Fixed by hand on the 14 machines tonight.

comments.author: p019
comments.text: Workstation image rebuilt with time sync on, and all 14 reinstalled. I added the clock thing to the login problems page.

summary: Dry run 2 failed: the copy to the cloud is 40 minutes behind
description:
Dry run 2 on 15 September was stopped at step 2.

- At 22:00 the cloud copy was 41 minutes behind the data centre
- The runbook allows 5 minutes at most before we stop writes
- During the day the delay is under 1 minute. It grows from 20:00, when the nightly renewal batch starts

With this delay, the cutover of 26 September is not possible.

comments.author: p022
comments.text: The link is not the problem: it runs at 30% during the batch. The cloud side applies changes with one worker, and the renewal batch writes faster than one worker can apply.

comments.author: p022
comments.text: Changed the sync to 8 parallel workers and gave the cloud database faster disks. Three nights in a row with the batch running: worst delay 2 min 10 s. Good enough for the 5-minute rule. Closing.

comments.author: p013
comments.text: Confirmed on my side. I will update the runbook next week.

summary: Add a manual approval step before production releases of Policy Admin
description:
After the cutover of the Policy Database, we want no surprise release of Policy Admin for a few weeks.

Request: from 16 November to 31 December, every production release of Policy Admin waits for a manual approval from me or from Amira.

Other systems are not concerned.

comments.author: p022
comments.text: Alexandre is on another project this month, so I took this one. First time I touch the pipeline config. The approval step works in the test pipeline. Still to do: limit it to Policy Admin and to the dates.
